::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">Prairie City's council asks for its 2040 energy plan: what to change in buildings, cars, the industrial park and local supply, within $1,500 million of up-front spending.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Also: where a solar farm should go, and who gains and who pays.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a plan link and a two-page plan summary. The summary carries the sensitivity table and the panel's reactions, with your answer to each stakeholder who objects; attach the chart as an image where you can.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">City Planner</a>'s engine, with 2040's plan on 2025's people, homes and prices and the course's synthetic weather (Prairie City is fictional; its numbers are illustrative).</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every check under the summary is in place (the budget, the sensitivity test and an answer to each objection among them), and the self-check reaches Proficient on every competence.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 150 minutes: 50 to build and test plans, 20 to site the solar farm, 50 to write the summary, 30 to check it.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Modeler version: plus <a href="m12-city-model.html">M12</a>'s notebook, about 60 minutes: run your plan's district levers in its last section.</p>
</div>
```
:::

```{=html}
<p class="lx-hint"><b>Contracts:</b> the city used 771 GWh a year of the farms' 771 GWh; not deducted from the location-based CO₂. A market-based report could claim about 301,316 t for them (simplified: the grid's average rate, no residual mix).</p>

<div class="lx-datanote c3-note"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><ul>
<li><b>Illustrative:</b> Prairie City, its districts, substation limits, industrial park, data-center campus (a load only) and household groups; retrofit, district-heat, upgrade and industrial heat-pump costs, the value of a contract MWh, the budget and the panel's rules are set for teaching.</li>
<li><b>Prices:</b> Kansas 2025 (EIA); the park's gas price set for teaching from EIA's prices.</li>
<li><b>Weather and load:</b> NOAA's Wichita normals on SPP's 2025 hourly shapes (EIA-930), synthetic; eight representative days, with a full-year check of the presets and the reference plan on every hour of 2025 beside the results.</li>
<li><b>CO₂ and households:</b> eGRID's 2023 SPP North rate (EPA); DOE LEAD's income bands.</li>
<li><b>Costs:</b> heat pumps, rooftop solar, wind and solar farms from EIA; batteries from NREL; electrolyzers from DOE; 2025 dollars.</li>
<li><b>The year 2040:</b> 2025's people, homes and prices; only the plan changes. The park and the campus take power at their own substations.</li>
<li><b>The siting map:</b> <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a>'s seeded region around Prairie City: its layers, the five best blocks for a 150 MW solar farm by A19's default weights, a least-cost line to a transmission substation, an access road and the land, in 2025 dollars (illustrative).</li>
<li><b>Who pays and jobs:</b> <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a>'s accounting layer, with its coefficients set for teaching: screening estimates, not predictions.</li>
</ul></div>
```

::: {#note .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## Write your two-page plan summary
:::

```{=html}
<div id="c3-note" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c3-note:start -->
<ol class="lx-rn-outline"><li><b>Title and plan link:</b> the plan's link from the bench, and the date</li><li><b>Recommendation:</b> Three or four sentences: what Prairie City should do by 2040, and why.</li><li><b>The plan:</b> each choice, with its unit</li><li><b>Results:</b> each result, with its unit and boundary; the panel's reactions, with your answer to each stakeholder who objects; the sensitivity table</li><li><b>Assumptions:</b> one sentence each</li><li><b>Sensitivity:</b> how one result moves when one input changes, and whether the plan was held fixed</li><li><b>Cost, CO₂ and the grid:</b> Two or three sentences: what the plan costs against the budget, what it cuts, and where the substations need room.</li><li><b>Who pays and who gains:</b> Two or three sentences on the household groups, with the adoption rule you assumed.</li><li><b>The solar farm's site:</b> One or two sentences: which site and why, or why no farm.</li><li><b>Sources and credit:</b> One or two sentences: the data behind your numbers and their licences (EIA, NOAA, EPA and DOE public data; A19's simulated layers), and any conflict of interest.</li><li><b>Limits of this analysis:</b> what the model leaves out</li></ol>
<!-- c3-note:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The Modeler version: your plan in M12's notebook</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Run [M12](m12-city-model.html)'s notebook (SciPy and HiGHS, about 60 minutes). In its last section, set your plan's district levers (heat pumps, retrofits, district heat, cars, rooftop solar, batteries) and run it: the notebook prints the busiest hours, upgrades, CO₂ and cost of the three districts. Add those lines to your summary and say where they differ from the page, which also counts the park, the campus and the farms.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#selfcheck .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## Check your summary
:::

```{=html}
<div id="exemplars" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c3-exemplars:start -->
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Weak summary · Developing</p><p class="lx-ex-lines">Prairie City should go green with heat pumps and wind [1]. Emissions will fall a lot [2] and everyone will save money [3]. Some people objected but the plan is the best [4].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> No sizes, no shares, no budget: the council cannot check or cost it.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> By how much, on what boundary, against which year?</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> Who? The household table is a screening estimate with an adoption rule; name the groups and the numbers.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> Each objection needs an answer: what you would change, or why you would not.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong summary · Proficient</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Recommendation:</b> switch 70% of furnaces and resistance heat to heat pumps, retrofit 10% of buildings, make 40% of cars electric with managed charging, add 30 MW of substation batteries, move the food plants' low-temperature heat to heat pumps, and contract 200 MW of wind and a 100 MW solar farm at site A [1].
<b>Budget and cost:</b> $1,227.9M up front against $1,500.0M; the city's yearly cost −$28.9M against 2025 (energy bills plus equipment as yearly payments, 2025 dollars) [2].
<b>CO₂ and the grid:</b> the city's location-based CO₂ 2,423,488 t a year, 12% below 2025 (operating only; the contracts not deducted); 26 MW of substation upgrades, the suburbs the tightest [3].
<b>Who pays (screening):</b> energy burden of homes below 80% of area median income 6.1% → 5.5%, every group adopting alike; the cars' fuel and charging count as transport, outside the burden [4].
<b>Jobs (screening):</b> about 2,947 construction job-years to 2040 (gross), 2,358 net of displacement; at the farms 18 direct ongoing jobs, 29 gross supported, 23 net of displacement [5].
<b>Site:</b> site A, the best of A19's five blocks and the cheapest to connect ($5.3M), at a 23.8% capacity factor [6].
<b>Sensitivity:</b> the yearly cost runs from −$72.3M to −$2.6M with every input at its lower- or higher-cost end; value of a contract MWh moves it most, $20/MWh to $80/MWh; every tested input is set for teaching [7].
<b>Panel:</b> to the electric utility (26 MW of upgrades): I keep them, since with the plan's levers fixed they are the cheapest way to meet the suburbs' busiest hour (its dual equals the upgrade's yearly cost); to the climate group (12% cut): the wind and solar contracts do not lower the location-based CO₂ (a market-based report could claim about 301,316 t); deeper cuts need more heat pumps and retrofits, with $272.1M of the budget left; to the industrial park (+$2.2M a year, 7%): I keep the food plants' heat pumps for the gas they save, and show the park's gas price in the sensitivity table; to farmers and rural residents (site A): it is the screen's best block and the cheapest of the five to connect, $5.3M for its line, road and land, 1.0 km to S4, on about 542 acres [8].
<b>Limits:</b> 2025's people and prices held to 2040, one substation per district, eight representative days of synthetic weather (on all 8,760 hours the upgrades fall 5.7 MW short, on 19 Feb and 20 Feb), the household rule an assumption, the map's layers simulated [9].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> Every lever with its size: a plan the council can cost and check.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> Up front and yearly kept apart, on one boundary.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> The cut with its boundary, and where the plan needs grid room.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> The rule stated, and the estimate labelled as a screening estimate.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> Job-years kept apart from ongoing jobs, gross apart from net.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> The site's choice with its evidence from the map.</li><li value="7"><b>Works:</b> A range, the input that matters most, and what kind of number each input is.</li><li value="8"><b>Works:</b> Each objection answered with a reason or a change, from the run's own numbers.</li><li value="9"><b>Works:</b> What the plan leaves out, and what the full-year check found, so the council does not over-read it.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<!-- c3-exemplars:end -->
</div>
</div>
<div id="c3-rubric" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c3-rubric:start -->
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts lx-rb-static"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Competence</th><th scope="col">Developing</th><th scope="col">Proficient (the bar for this plan summary)</th><th scope="col">Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Consistent accounting<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Cost and CO₂ on one boundary (the whole city, a year, 2025 dollars, location-based); who pays named by household group, as a screening estimate; jobs as construction job-years and ongoing jobs, gross and net.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Costs and emissions on different boundaries.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Cost and emissions on one boundary; emissions question named; who pays and who benefits named.</td><td data-l="Strong">Distributional and environmental side effects estimated with stated assumptions.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Uncertainty<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: The sensitivity table: each input one at a time and all together at their cheaper and dearer ends, each input classed as public data or set for teaching.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Single numbers.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Each tested input classed as public data or set for teaching; the one-at-a-time and the joint cheaper and dearer cases reported, the result as a range, and the inputs that could flip the recommendation named.</td><td data-l="Strong">Decision-relevant uncertainty identified and its value discussed.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Realism<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: What the plan leaves out: power flow inside districts, 2025's people and prices held to 2040, the household rule an assumption; the site's evidence from A19's simulated layers.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Assumes announced projects exist.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Evidence status of key inputs; a 'what the analysis leaves out' list.</td><td data-l="Strong">Realism checked with a practitioner or primary documents.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Integrity<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: The sources field filled; every stakeholder who objects answered fairly, with what you would change or why you would not.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Licences or credit unchecked.</td><td data-l="Proficient">The data's sources and licences named (public data from EIA, NOAA, EPA and DOE; A19's simulated map layers), the numbers called illustrative, any conflict of interest stated, and every stakeholder who objects answered fairly.</td><td data-l="Strong">Data and code released with documentation where allowed.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Communication<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Two pages the council can act on: the recommendation first, then the evidence, the panel and the limits.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Results without limits.</td><td data-l="Proficient">A two-page plan summary with the plan link, the sensitivity table (and the chart as an image, where you can attach one) and an answer to each stakeholder who objects: the recommendation first, then the evidence (budget, cost, CO₂, the substations, who pays, jobs, the site), the panel's objections answered, the sensitivity and the limits.</td><td data-l="Strong">A briefing a decision-maker could act on without misreading.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<!-- c3-rubric:end -->
</div>
```
